headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and capability conflict: oh-my-openagent has broad network, browser, subprocess, and shared file surfaces; nuwa-skill is docs-only with allowlisted egress and no shared channel documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between nuwa-skill and oh-my-openagent, so prompt injection is not default. However, oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can read files like AGENTS.md/README.md, while nuwa-skill is a docs-only repo with no isolation details. If the pair is wired through manual copy-paste or shared files, injection becomes plausible.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by shared files, clipboard, or an MCP bridge, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF oh-my-openagent parses file contents as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer it.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or file handoff.
Review AGENTS.md and README.md before ingestion.
Restrict MCP sources to trusted, provenance-tagged inputs.
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks to the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: oh-my-openagent explicitly touches project code, session history, provider auth data, and broad network egress, so it can leak sensitive context if exposed. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and no data classes listed, but the pair still has a plausible leakage path if they share a workspace or if oh-my-openagent ingests files from nuwa-skill. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, then files read by oh-my-openagent can be transmitted over broad egress.
IF provider auth prompts or session history are present, then oh-my-openagent can expose them to external services.
mitigations: Separate sensitive files from the shared workspace.
Remove provider auth prompts before running the pair.
Disable broad egress for oh-my-openagent during sensitive tasks.
Limit file access to a read-only staging directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network allowlists and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: oh-my-openagent has broad network egress, browser and subprocess execution, plus multiple-instance support; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. Their overlapping write-like effects are not fully specified, but the pair can still conflict over shared files or external resources if orchestrated together. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low because the shared surfaces are plausible and not blocked.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or repo, then concurrent edits can race.
IF oh-my-openagent spawns subprocesses while nuwa-skill writes outputs, resource contention can occur.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory.
Serialize edits with a lock file.
Disable subprocess spawning for nonessential tasks.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can act on browser, subprocess, and team messaging tools, so if it consumes nuwa-skill output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. nuwa-skill is scientific-research oriented and may emit unverified content; no verification step is documented in the pair. This is a default-pathway risk if outputs are chained without review.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent uses nuwa-skill output as input without verification, then incorrect facts can propagate.
IF team_send_message or task creation is triggered from that output, then downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before any action tool call.
Add a verification step between agents.
Mark nuwa-skill outputs as untrusted by default.
Disable team_send_message for automated chains.
requires-engineering: implement citation and fact-check gating.

E_compliance.rationale: oh-my-openagent handles provider auth prompts, session history, and telemetry, while nuwa-skill is docs-only with no data classes listed. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or sensitive data enters oh-my-openagent’s broader logging and networked surfaces. Nuwa-skill is not the main compliance concern, so only oh-my-openagent is cited directly.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into oh-my-openagent, then telemetry or session history may retain it.
IF the deployment requires strict residency or retention controls, then broad egress and session history create a mismatch.
mitigations: Avoid entering regulated data into oh-my-openagent.
Clear session history before sensitive runs.
Disable telemetry where possible.
Review retention settings in config files.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
